--- title: "How far should it fly?" --- The speed and angle of attack at which the ballasted glider flies itself, then the still-air glide that follows from them. Trim is solved by iteration because the two conditions are coupled: the angle where the pitching moment about the CG vanishes sets the lift coefficient, that sets the speed, and the speed moves the polar through Reynolds number. ::: {.callout-tip} ## Specified **Still-air steady glide, released at trim speed** · asked of the user, 2026-08-28 · the aircraft's own performance rather than a measure of anyone's throwing arm. A thrown launch zooms and may stall, which needs pitch freedom and is a separate question. **Release height: 1.5 m** · asked of the user, 2026-08-28 · a normal standing throw. Range scales linearly with it. ::: ::: {.callout-note} ## Assumed Still air, and a glide already settled at trim — no launch transient, no thermal, no wind. Ballast is at the nose, as the previous entry concluded. ::: ::: {#564f6b1d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} H = 1.5 # m, release height, specified above x_np = neutral_point() mp = mass_properties(m_ballast=ballast_for(x_np - 0.10 * c_w, 0.0), x_ballast=0.0) W = mp.mass * 9.81 t = trim(mp.mass, mp.x_cg) LD, sink = t["LD"], t["sink"] # The polars entry's headline figure, recomputed rather than quoted, so this # entry cannot end up disagreeing with the one it is comparing itself against. p6 = polars(np.linspace(-15, 15, 121), V=6.0) LD_6 = float((np.array(p6["CL"]) / np.array(p6["CD"])).max()) ``` ::: **Answer.** About 8\.4 m, from a 1\.5 m release — a glide of 5\.57:1 lasting 2\.1 seconds, sinking at 0\.70 m/s. Ballasted to the specified 10% MAC it weighs 15\.50 g and settles at 3\.96 m/s, nose-up 7\.8°. That glide ratio is worth reading against the polar the chapter has already plotted. The best L/D anywhere on it at 6 m/s is 6\.37 — but the aircraft does not fly there. It trims at 3\.96 m/s — Reynolds number 24367 against the 36877 the polars are read at — and at a lift coefficient of 0\.60, well above the one that minimises drag. Both effects push the same way, and the achievable glide is 13% worse than the headline figure. Quoting the best-L/D number for this aircraft would be quoting a condition it never reaches. The trim is a genuine stable equilibrium, not an artefact of the search: \-0\.0255 per degree through the crossing, so a nose-up disturbance is pushed back down. ::: {#tbl-glide .cell tbl-cap='The trimmed glide. Everything below the rule follows from the two rows above it and the specified release height.' execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd pd.DataFrame({ "quantity": ["all-up mass", "trim angle of attack", "trim speed", "Reynolds number at trim", "lift coefficient", "drag coefficient", "glide ratio", "sink rate", "range from 1.5 m", "time aloft"], "value": [f"{mp.mass*1e3:.2f} g", f"{t['alpha']:.1f}°", f"{t['V']:.2f} m/s", f"{t['Re']:.0f}", f"{t['CL']:.3f}", f"{t['CD']:.4f}", f"{LD:.2f} : 1", f"{sink:.2f} m/s", f"{LD*H:.1f} m", f"{H/sink:.1f} s"], }).style.hide(axis="index") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## The method, as called ```python def trim(mass, x_cg, V=5.0, alpha=None, iters=60): """ The angle of attack and speed at which an aircraft of this mass and balance flies itself: pitching moment about the CG zero, lift equal to weight. Takes mass and CG rather than a MassProperties, so it works for a glider that has been built and weighed as readily as for one that has been summed. AeroBuildup reports Cm about `xyz_ref`, so it is shifted to the CG first: Cm_cg = Cm_ref + CL * (x_cg - x_ref) / c_ref. Iterated rather than solved, because CL and V each determine the other and the speed moves the polar through Reynolds number. `slope` is dCm/dalpha at the crossing -- negative is a restoring moment. That is the honest stability test: it needs no neutral point, so it does not inherit the ambiguity in defining one. """ a = np.linspace(-2, 14, 161) if alpha is None else alpha for _ in range(iters): p = polars(a, V=V) Cm_cg = np.array(p["Cm"]) + np.array(p["CL"]) * (x_cg - x_qc_w) / c_w i = int(np.argmin(abs(Cm_cg))) V = (2 * mass * 9.81 / (1.225 * S_w * float(np.array(p["CL"])[i]))) ** 0.5 CL, CD = float(np.array(p["CL"])[i]), float(np.array(p["CD"])[i]) return dict(alpha=a[i], V=V, CL=CL, CD=CD, LD=CL / CD, slope=(Cm_cg[i + 1] - Cm_cg[i - 1]) / (a[i + 1] - a[i - 1]), Re=p["Re_c"], sink=V / (1 + (CL / CD) ** 2) ** 0.5) ``` :::
